Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the SIG partial we received last week. Our security team reviewed your answers and has a couple of follow-ups specifically around access controls: SSO/SAML configuration options, SCIM provisioning (delta vs. full), RBAC model and how roles are mapped, and MFA enforcement.

Can you:
- Confirm whether Redwood supports SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML flows and provide an example metadata file.
- Describe SCIM v2 support and whether you support group push and delta syncs (we need to know if group membership changes propagate).
- Provide a short explanation of the RBAC implementation: default roles, how custom roles are created, and whether role assignment can be managed via SCIM.
- Clarify where MFA is enforced (at IdP vs. local accounts) and whether there are enforcement exceptions for service accounts.

If possible, please attach configuration examples and an access-control mapping CSV. We may also want a brief 30-min call with your security lead this week.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our audit window is next week.

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: we need access controls detail and evidence

Hi Danielle —

Thanks — we can absolutely provide these. High level answers first, attachments + short notes following.

1) SAML/SSO
- We support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML flows.
- We publish an SP metadata file (attached: redwood_saml_metadata.xml) that contains the ACS URLs, entityID, and signed assertion settings.
- We support signed assertions and encrypted NameID where required; we can toggle required attributes via the Console.

2) SCIM
- Redwood implements SCIM 2.0 for user and group provisioning. We support create/update/delete and delta syncs for users and groups.
- Group push is supported: group membership changes made in the IdP will be propagated to Redwood during the next delta sync.
- Our SCIM endpoint supports paging and incremental sync by returning 'startIndex'/'totalResults' and using 'if-modified-since' headers for efficiency.

3) RBAC
- RBAC is role-based with a small set of system roles (admin, editor, viewer) and support for custom roles scoped to an account.
- Default new users are assigned the 'viewer' role by default to enforce least privilege.
- Role assignment can be managed via SCIM: we map SCIM's 'groups' and an attribute 'roles' to internal roles. See access-control-matrix.csv for examples.

4) MFA and service accounts
- MFA enforcement is at the IdP level for SSO users (we recommend IdP-enforced MFA).
- We do not permit local password-based accounts by default for production tenants; local console accounts are disabled unless explicitly provisioned and approved by an account admin.
- Service accounts use API keys or mTLS certificates; they are excluded from human MFA flows but are scoped to least-privilege API roles and are audited.

I'll attach the SP metadata, a SCIM quick-start/config guide, and an access-control matrix. If you want a short call, Vivek (cc'd) is our Security Lead and can do a 30-min slot tomorrow afternoon.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Manager, Enterprise Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Danielle / Acme team —

Quick technical clarifications from the security side:
- Assertion attributes: we support mapping for email, username, groups, and a custom 'roles' attribute if your IdP can emit it.
- SCIM provisioning: provisioning is transactional; when a group update arrives we apply the delta and log the specific user membership changes to the audit log (available via Console and export).
- RBAC enforcement: permission checks are evaluated at API edge and within the Console; tokens issued for API keys are constrained by role claims.
- MFA: for SSO users, MFA checks are performed by the IdP during authentication. For audit purposes, we capture and surface the identity provider used and the authentication method in session metadata.

If you'd like, we can redact a sample audit log entry showing a group membership delta and the resulting role changes — that's useful for auditors.

Vivek
Head of Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Danielle —

Thanks — confirmed:
- Canonical SCIM role attribute: we accept 'roles' (string array) and will also accept 'entitlements' (we normalize to internal role IDs). If you plan to use group-based mapping, include the group displayName that maps to the role in the access-control CSV.
- API key rotation: recommended cadence is 90 days for long-lived keys. We support automated rotation for service principals via our Management API (POST /v1/keys/rotate) for customers on Dedicated/Private plans; for hosted tenants we can initiate rotation and assist via support if desired.
- Attached: redacted_audit_example.txt (excerpt) which shows a group delta sync where 'engineering-backend' lost one member and the resulting role reduction from 'editor' to 'viewer' for that user.

We'll plan the 11:00am PST call tomorrow; Vivek and I will be on the line and can share screens to walk through the Console SCIM logs. Meeting invite to follow.
